articles.headline: Williams connects with Loveland to set up Santos' winning field goal as Bears edge Buccaneers 27-24
articles.description: — Caleb Williams and the Chicago Bears played one of their worst games of the season — and won.
articles.body:
CHICAGO -- — Caleb Williams and the Chicago Bears played one of their worst games of the season — and won.


              That last part was the only thing that mattered to them Sunday night.


              Williams found Colston Loveland for a 38-yard reception that set up Cairo Santos' 38-yard field goal as time expired, and the Bears picked up a sloppy 27-24 victory over Baker Mayfield and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.


              Chicago (7-2) committed five turnovers, including a career-high four interceptions by Williams. But he delivered after Mayfield rallied the Buccaneers in the final minutes.


              “I don’t get gun shy. That’s not me. That’s not my identity,” Williams said. “And with that, I’m going to keep ripping it and keep ripping it.”


              With Chicago facing a second-and-9 from its own 46 in the final minute, Williams passed to a wide-open Loveland at the Tampa Bay 35. The tight end ran down the sideline before he was pushed out of bounds at the 16.


              After two kneel-downs by Williams, Santos delighted the crowd of 60,470 by drilling his second field goal of the night.


              It was Chicago's first win with five-plus turnovers since a 23-13 victory over the Minnesota Vikings on Dec. 3, 2006.


              “It’s hard to win with five turnovers and yet we found a way to do it,” Bears coach Ben Johnson said. “They know that we didn't play as well as we’re capable of playing but I believe the best is yet to come in terms of our football in the back half of the season. So we’ll continue to build that as we go forward.” 


              Chicago had a 24-16 lead when Luther Burden fumbled on a helmet-to-helmet hit by Tampa Bay rookie Rueben Bain Jr. Bucs defensive back Ifeatu Melifonwu returned the ball to the Bears 17.


              Bucky Irving had an 11-yard carry before going in from the 6 for his second touchdown of the game. Mayfield scrambled for the 2-point conversion, tying it at 24 with 2:51 left.


              Mayfield was 18 for 32 for 243 yards and two interceptions. Irving finished with 97 yards on 20 carries.


              Mayfield failed to complete a pass in Tampa Bay’s previous game, a 16-0 win over Atlanta in wet conditions. The Buccaneers (3-6) rushed for a franchise-record 324 yards in the victory over the Falcons, including 170 by Irving.


              Williams was 22 for 37 for 279 yards and two touchdowns in Chicago’s fourth straight win. Burden had seven catches for 97 yards before he was shelved by a concussion. Jeffery Simmons had a sack in his first home game since he was acquired in a trade with Tennessee.


              The Buccaneers and Bears were the NFL’s top rushing teams going into the weekend, but there wasn’t much room to maneuver on the ground. The Bucs finished with 126 yards rushing, and the Bears had 72.

articles.headline: NFL Week 9: Big takeaways, questions and fantasy spin from Sunday's games
articles.description: Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering the biggest questions coming out of each Sunday game. Here's what we learned from Week 9.
articles.body:
The Sunday slate for Week 9 of the 2026 NFL season kicked off in Madrid with the Bengals' offense erupting in a win over the Falcons. Cincinnati wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase finished with a season-high 155 yards and a touchdown on 10 receptions.

Back in the United States, Rams edge rusher Myles Garrett returned from injury, finishing with three sacks in a win over the Commanders. Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders fell to the Saints in his first start of the 2026 season. And quarterback Bo Nix led the Broncos to their fifth fourth-quarter comeback this year -- tied for the most through nine games in NFL history, per the Elias Sports Bureau.

Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering lingering questions coming out of each game -- including how teams will approach Tuesday's trade deadline. Fantasy football analysts Matt Bowen and Tristan Cockcroft also have fantasy takeaways from each matchup.

Let's get to it with the biggest lessons from Sunday.

Jump to:

DAL-IND | CLE-NO | NYG-PHI

NYJ-KC | DEN-CAR | LAR-WSH

DET-MIA | CIN-ATL

Catch up on Thursday's game:

JAX-BAL

Dallas 27, Indianapolis 23

Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Cowboys

Should the Cowboys make a trade at the deadline? At 4-5, the Cowboys have one fewer win than the NFC East-leading Giants (5-2-1), so they are still in the division race ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline. As tempting as it might be, owner and general manager Jerry Jones said on the 105.3 The Fan pregame show Sunday, "At this point, I don't see it." The Cowboys made their big trade already for CB Joey Porter Jr. and don't have a ton of assets to make a substantive move. Would it really make a difference? If they want to replicate 2018, when they started 3-5 and made the playoffs after trading for WR Amari Cooper, it will likely be with the current roster.

Trend to watch: The Cowboys' defense looked competent in the first half for the second straight game. Against Arizona, they allowed 129 yards and no TDs. Against the Colts, they allowed a touchdown but only 79 yards -- the fewest by Dallas in a first half since Week 18 of 2024 against the Commanders. -- Todd Archer

Next game: vs. 49ers (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

Colts

Will Sunday's loss impact trade deadline decisions? The Colts have been heavily involved in trade discussions since GM Chris Ballard was fired last month; they've already traded away guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner. But the word around the team Sunday was that the Colts were less likely to make a splashy deal than to do one. Still, falling to 2-7 and suffering a fifth straight loss could impact principal owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon's thinking. Running back Jonathan Taylor and wide receiver Josh Downs are among the most discussed trade possibilities, and quarterback Daniel Jones is a more remote possibility.

articles.headline: Titans WR Calvin Ridley involved in incident at Nashville airport
articles.description: Titans WR Calvin Ridley was involved in an incident at Nashville International Airport over the weekend, details of which have not been released.
articles.body:
NASHVILLE, Tenn. -- Tennessee Titans wide receiver Calvin Ridley was involved in an incident at Nashville International Airport over the weekend, the Metropolitan Nashville Airport Authority confirmed Sunday night.

Details of the incident haven't been released. Tennessee had a bye this week. 

The Titans are aware of the situation but have not provided any further comment as of Sunday night. They are in communication with the Metropolitan Nashville Airport Authority.

Titans coach Robert Saleh is scheduled to speak to the local media Monday at 8:15 am CT.

Ridley signed a four-year, $92 million contract with the Titans in 2024. The veteran receiver has six receptions for 91 yards through seven games this season.

articles.headline: Giants' Malik Nabers takes issue with Greg Olsen, Fox for comments during game
articles.description: Malik Nabers took issue with Fox play-by-play man Joe Davis and analyst Greg Olsen for criticizing his body language during the Giants' win Sunday.
articles.body:
Malik Nabers was happy with the Giants' win Sunday but not happy with how the Fox telecast portrayed him during it.

In a social media post after the team's 19-11 victory over the Eagles in Philadelphia, Nabers took issue with Fox play-by-play man Joe Davis and analyst Greg Olsen, who criticized the third-year receiver's body language at times during the game.

"Yall be trying [to] create a narrative on me soo bad, it's actually crazy. If you [don't] like the way I play the game, keep the camera off me!! SIMPLE!" he wrote as part of an Instagram story.

"But [Olsen] calling me a bad teammate when every team I've been on, there's NOBODY I've played with has said dat bout me is crazy!

"My face the same way if I'm having a good game, bad, winning or losing. If it's a problem: 1. Keep the camera off of me. 2. Pray bout it! Simple."

Nabers had five catches on eight targets for 43 yards in the win, the first time since Week 3 that he has been held to fewer than 100 yards.

With the Giants nursing a 13-8 lead and driving early in the fourth quarter, New York quarterback J.J. McCarthy threw behind Nabers for an incompletion, with replays later showing the receiver waving the air and Olsen telling viewers that was a sign that he wanted the ball thrown more in front of him.

"His body language has been terrible today," Davis said.

Olsen then quickly added: "It's just not good."

The conversation continued around Nabers and his body language, with Davis questioning why he didn't look more positive after Isaiah Likely scored a go-ahead TD for New York earlier in the second half.

"Yeah, listen, there's a fine line," Olsen said. "I've played with a lot of really good wide receivers. ... There's never been a great wide receiver who hasn't demanded the ball. That kind of comes with the territory. There are a few exceptions of guys that are just a different personality and a different approach.

"But there is a very fine line between being demanding, being a competitor and all of those great things. That's great. It just can never cross [that line] where it feels like it takes away from the success of your teammates. So when your teammate catches a wide-open touchdown, you need to be the happiest guy on the field. You can't still be worried about your targets. That's the fine line. He's a talented young, really good player. He's just got to keep it in check."

Shortly after, Nabers laid out for a third-down McCarthy pass in the end zone but couldn't come up with it.

"Listen, you want to demand the ball; you can't throw that ball any better," Olsen said. "That's a touchdown. You're a premier player in this league. You've got an opportunity there, you've got to catch it."

The Giants instead settled for a field goal to go ahead 16-8 with about nine minutes left in the game.

articles.headline: Golden State Warriors guard Will Richard sidelined with torn ligament in thumb
articles.description: Second-year Golden State Warriors guard Will Richard, who has been providing key minutes as both a starter and a reserve, has a torn ligament in his left thumb that will sideline him for an undetermined stretch.
articles.body:
SAN FRANCISCO -- Second-year Golden State Warriors guard Will Richard has a torn ligament in his left thumb that will sideline him for an undetermined stretch.

The Warriors listed Richard on the injury report Sunday with a torn ulnar collateral ligament and he was out for Monday's game against New Orleans at Chase Center as the team concludes a six-game homestand. Golden State didn't have practice or media availability Sunday, so there wasn't an immediate timetable for Richard's recovery or a known treatment plan.

Richard has been providing key minutes as both a starter and a reserve as Golden State has won seven straight games since an 0-3 start. He made two starts this past week, against Phoenix and Miami.

Stephen Curry has credited the Warriors figuring out their roles to grab some momentum after dropping the first three games.

"Everybody having an impact, throw Will Richard in there, too, he's had three straight games really where he's turned up the energy defensively for us," Curry said after a 116-113 win over the Suns on Monday. "Defensively, he's just been a pest out there."

The 23-year-old guard was a second-round draft pick last year out of Florida after he led the Gators to a national championship.

Richard is averaging 5.1 points, 1.8 rebounds and 1.0 assists while shooting 47.5% from the floor and 42.9% from 3-point range.

Sacramento Kings forward Keegan Murray dealt with the same injury early last season, underwent surgery and missed the first 15 games.

articles.headline: Giannis Antetokounmpo scores 29 points to lead the Heat to a 114-108 win over the struggling Kings
articles.description: — Giannis Antetokounmpo had 29 points, 14 rebounds, and three assists in the Miami Heat’s 114-108 win over the Sacramento Kings on Sunday.
articles.body:
SACRAMENTO, Calif. -- — Giannis Antetokounmpo had 29 points, 14 rebounds, and three assists in the Miami Heat’s 114-108 win over the Sacramento Kings on Sunday.


              Antetokounmpo made 14 of 23 shots from the field and added three assists and two blocks. 


              Klay Thompson had 23 points, including seven 3-pointers, for the Heat (4-6), and Bam Adebayo added 18 points and eight rebounds.


              Darius Acuff Jr. had 32 points and 10 assists for the Kings (1-9), who have not won a home game. 


              The game was tied at 55-all until the Heat went on a 13-4 run, capped by two free throws by Adebayo at the 55-second mark of the second quarter. The Heat led 68-59 at the half. Adebayo, Antetokounmpo, and Davion Mitchell combined for 41 of the Heat’s first-half points. 


              The Heat got the lead up to 16 points in the third quarter, before the Kings surged back to tie the game at 95 on two free throws by De’Andre Hunter at the 6:12 mark of the fourth. 


              The Heat regained the lead and outscored the Kings 19-13 the rest of the way for the victory. 


              Domantas Sabonis did not play for the Kings due to left knee soreness. 


              The Kings announced that the team traded second-year wing Nique Clifford to the Oklahoma City Thunder. In return, the Kings received Utah’s 2028 second-round draft pick and Minnesota’s 2030 second-round draft pick.


              Clifford was selected in the first round (24th overall pick) of the 2025 NBA draft by the Thunder, who traded his draft rights to the Kings.


              Up next
              Kings: Host Orlando on Tuesday night.


              Heat: At Utah on Tuesday night.

Nov. 6: Jaguars overwhelm Ravens, underwhelm fantasy managers

By Adam Rank

The Jaguars have totaled 702 points in 25 games under head coach Liam Coen after hanging 33 on the Ravens on Thursday night. Coen is now tied for the third-fastest to reach 700 points, trailing just Mike Martz (22) and Sean McVay (23). I really love watching the way the Jaguars methodically take teams apart, but let's be honest, many of you did not enjoy the game, sticking around only to watch Al Michaels allude to betting lines. 

But despite all of the points being scored, whom can we rely on consistently for fantasy purposes? Trevor Lawrence played great. He scored only 13.58 fantasy points. Bhayshul Tuten got into the end zone early in this one. He finished in single digits. And the Jaguars added insult to fantasy injury by giving yet another touchdown to Chris Rodriguez Jr.  The leading scorer on the night?  It was Ravens RB Justice Hill, almost entirely on a meaningless fourth quarter 65-yard touchdown. He was started in fewer than 2% of leagues. The scoring leader for the Jaguars? Kicker Cam Little.  Even the defense outscored every other Jaguar who wasn't throwing or kicking the ball.

The lone saving grace was Parker Washington. However, he's been marred by inconsistency in recent weeks, turning in a positive performance on Thursday night only after almost a third of his managers left him on the bench (please don't let that have been you). 

The point is, there is no way we're sitting Tuten or (in hindsight) Washington in the coming weeks. You don't sit players in prolific offenses. But the consistency might not be there. Buckle up.

articles.headline: Clippers beat Pelicans to end 7-game losing streak
articles.description: — Darius Garland had 24 points and 10 assists, Brook Lopez added 20 points and the Los Angeles Clippers ended a seven-game losing streak with a 139-123 victory over the New Orleans Pelicans on Sunday night.
articles.body:
INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- — Darius Garland had 24 points and 10 assists, Brook Lopez added 20 points and the Los Angeles Clippers ended a seven-game losing streak with a 139-123 victory over the New Orleans Pelicans on Sunday night.


              Gradey Dick and rookie Keaton Wagler each scored 15 points and Rui Hachimura added 14 as the Clippers won for the first time since getting past the Sacramento Kings in the season opener.


              The Clippers went on a 15-6 run to open the fourth quarter to take control with a 117-101 lead and finished off the victory after failing to hold on to double-digit fourth-quarter leads in their previous two games.


              Trey Murphy III scored 26 points, while Zion Williamson and Jeremiah Fears each added 25 as the Pelicans lost their second consecutive game following a four-game winning streak. Saddiq Bey had 13 points for New Orleans, which was playing the opener of a two-game California trip.


              The Pelicans shot 50.6% from the floor while getting held to 52 points in the paint after entering the with 61.6 per game in that department to lead the NBA.


              The Clippers took a 124-107 lead with 4:56 remaining on three free throws from Garland and cruised to the victory from there with a season high in points. Los Angeles shot a season-best 54.8% from the floor.


              The Clippers led 67-60 at halftime after shooting 52.3% from the floor and getting 14 points from Garland, while Williamson had 17 points for the Pelicans. New Orleans opened the second half on an 18-10 run to take their first lead since the opening minute at 78-77.


              Los Angeles was without center Isaiah Jackson (groin), as well as former Pelicans star Brandon Ingram (heel), who is close to his debut for his new team.


              Up next
              Pelicans: At Golden State on Monday night.


              Clippers: At Phoenix on Tuesday night.

articles.headline: Reaves scores 43 in Doncic's absence to lead Lakers past Pistons
articles.description: Austin Reaves did his best Luka Doncic impression with the MVP candidate resting vs. the Pistons on Sunday, scoring 43 points in the 121-116 win.
articles.body:
DETROIT -- If Austin Reaves' season-high 43 points in the Los Angeles Lakers' 121-116 win over the Detroit Pistons wasn't enough of a Luka Doncic impersonation, Reaves made sure to fully embody his teammate on a 3-pointer he hoisted up in the third quarter Sunday.

"Honestly, when I stepped back and shot it, I was like, 'This is some bulls--- Luka would shoot,'" Reaves said.

The shot ricocheted off the glass and through the hoop and was one of many that fell for him -- he shot 14-of-27 from the field (4-of-6 from 3) and 11-for-11 from the foul line -- as L.A. extended its winning streak to five despite Doncic missing the game because of tightness in his lower back.

"I didn't try to bank it in," Reaves said, explaining why he shrugged his shoulders in disbelief afterward. "It went in, so it looks the same in the stat sheet."

And the Lakers (9-2) looked like the same confident group they've been to start the season, despite playing without Doncic, the NBA's No. 1 scorer (40.1 points per game), against a Pistons team ranked No. 1 in defense.

 

"Guys have to step up when someone's averaging 40," said Lakers guard Collin Sexton, who scored 17 points off the bench. "You got to fill the shoes and be ready to impact winning. And I felt like we did that tonight, and AR picked those shoes up and he wore them."

It was the second game that Doncic has missed this season -- both because of back tightness and in a back-to-back scenario (L.A. continues its four-game road stretch in Atlanta on Monday). The Lakers are 2-0 without him.

"I thought AR's decision-making, his aggression, his ability to just consistently touch the paint and get downhill was fantastic tonight," Lakers coach JJ Redick said of Reaves.

L.A. had five players score in double digits, with Reaves and Sexton joined by Ziaire Williams (17 points off the bench), Walker Kessler (12 points, 16 rebounds, 3 blocks) and Quentin Grimes, who scored 10 of his 12 points in the first quarter when the Lakers built a 38-14 lead.

Detroit (6-3) chipped away, outscoring L.A. by eight from the 2:30 mark of the third until the 9:14 mark of the fourth with Reaves resting on the bench to draw within one, down 90-89.

Redick explained why he didn't sub Reaves, who had already played 28 of 33 minutes when he exited, back in the game quicker.

"You got to allow the players to play through it," Redick said. "And the same thing with the star players, you got to allow them to get their rest. And if you start just overreacting in-game and saying, 'I got to get this guy back in, I got to get this guy back in,' it's just chaos. And we're trying to create consistency for our players."

Redick downplayed any concern he has about Doncic's back being a lingering injury, so L.A.'s starting backcourt will likely be together again in Atlanta. But for a night at least, the Lakers had another 40-point scorer leading the way.

articles.headline: Fermín López delivers brace as Barcelona defeat Atlético Madrid
articles.description: Sam Marsden describes a stunning performance from Fermín López as Barcelona secure a 2-1 win over Atlético Madrid.

articles.headline: Diego Simeone: Atlético Madrid need Julián Álvarez at his 'best' to succeed
articles.description: Diego Simeone says Atlético Madrid will give Julián Álvarez time to re-discover his best form after the striker missed a string of chances in Sunday's 2-1 defeat to Barcelona at the Metropolitano.
articles.body:
MADRID -- Diego Simeone says Atlético Madrid will give Julián Álvarez time to re-discover his best form after the striker missed a string of chances in Sunday's 2-1 defeat to Barcelona at the Metropolitano.

Álvarez set up the opening goal for Giuliano Simeone but couldn't convert his own opportunities as two Fermín López strikes earned victory for the side the Argentina forward wanted to join in the summer.

This was the first time Atlético have faced Barça since Álvarez revealed he wanted to leave in June, something he has since apologised to the club's supporters for.

 

"Julián had a good game," Atlético coach Simeone said in the post-match news conference. "As well as the chances he had, he was also involved in several other attacking moves.

"On top of setting up Giuliano's goal, he also delivered a cross for [an Alex] Baena [chance]. We all wanted him to get that goal, but we'll be patient with him because he's a great player.

"We love him and, if we're going to achieve what we want to achieve, we need Julián at his best -- otherwise we won't get there."

Álvarez was jeered by Atlético supporters at the start of the season for trying to engineer a move to Barça.

As a result, Simeone managed his minutes more carefully at times, but he has now started Atlético's last five games in all competitions, scoring twice.

His misses against Barça were in contrast to Fermín's finishing. The midfielder took both of his goals really well as the Catalan side ensured they go into the international break as league leaders.

"It was an extraordinary performance," Simeone added, despite the loss. "I cannot fault the players. It was the game we wanted to play, pressing well in the first half with good intensity.

"On this occasion, we were not as clinical as we have been on other days. Barça are very good in that sense. They had fewer clear chances, but were clinical with the ones they had."

In an action-packed start to the game, Álvarez wasted a on- on-one with Joan García and Marc Pubill and Pedri hit woodwork at either end before Simeone opened the scoring in the 10th minute.

Álvarez saw another effort saved by García as Atlético pushed for a second but they were caught cold by Fermín's strike just before the break.

"The 1-1 was very important before half time," Barça coach Hansi Flick said in the post-match news conference.

"In the first half, we were too far from the opponent, so it wasn't easy to get pressure on the ball. They always switched [play on] us; this is what we made much better in the second half."

The introduction of Frenkie de Jong helped Barça improve, although Álvarez still had more chances, lifting a lob on to the roof of the net and having another shot deflected over.

Fermín was not so wasteful, finishing brilliantly to seal the points in the 66th minute after latching on to a brilliant Lamine Yamal pass.

"You play 90 minutes," Flick added. "The first half was not so perfect. The second half was good and we deserve this win.

articles.headline: Barça pass their biggest test yet as Fermín López sinks Atlético Madrid
articles.description: Needing a response after losing to Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid, Barcelona came from behind at Atlético on Sunday to underline their title credentials.
articles.body:
MADRID -- Fermín López produced two finishes of the highest quality as Barcelona came from behind to beat Atlético Madrid 2-1 on Sunday at the Metropolitano to claim their biggest win of the season so far.

It was a victory which was much needed after back-to-back defeats to Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid in October. Barça had scored 60 goals in 15 games -- an average of four per match -- heading into this weekend's trip to Atlético, but those losses had raised question marks about whether they could step up against better opposition when it really matters.

Those questions may return at some point -- Atlético were the better side in the first half -- but Hansi Flick's side's reaction to those setbacks has been good. After hammering Alavés in LaLiga and beating Aston Villa in the UEFA Champions League, victory against Diego Simeone's side ensured they remain the top of the league. With 11 wins from 12 games, they have a three-point cushion over Real Madrid, while Atlético are now five points back.

- Anthony Gordon left Premier League to get 'respect' -- he's got it now

- Man Utd's poor starts have Premier League relegation looking more likely

- Liverpool's Barcola, Isak, Wirtz show signs they're finally starting to click

The build-up to Sunday's game was dripping with narrative. Last season's meetings between the two teams were still very much present. Barça beat Atlético twice in LaLiga en route to back-to-back titles only to suffer painful eliminations to the Rojiblancos in the Copa del Rey and, especially, the Champions League.

However, the main focus was on Julián Álvarez. This was the first time the two teams had met since the Atleti striker tried to engineer a summer transfer to Barça. He missed several chances here, although he did set up the early opener for Giuliano Simeone.

Before the game, the home fans unveiled a giant tifo with the words "Mi dulce condena" -- "My sweet sentence" -- alongside an anonymous Atlético player behind bars. It felt like a nod to Álvarez being reluctantly forced to stay at the club after saying it would "be best for everyone" if a transfer could be agreed.

In a fast-paced start to the game, the Argentina international had a great early chance to make amends by opening the scoring. One-on-one with Joan García, he attempted to round the Barça goalkeeper, but was forced too wide and the chance was gone. Marc Pubill thumped the bar from the resulting corner; Pedri then hit the woodwork at the other end. This was all within seven minutes.

Three minutes later, Atlético led. A simple switch of play caused Barça's defence all sorts of problems, Álvarez squared and Simeone, who had lost João Cancelo, turned home.

Álvarez, after another Cancelo mistake, then saw another effort stopped by García, the ball snaking towards the line after the save but cleared by Barça eventually.

Barça grew into the game before the break, but there was still an element of surprise about their equaliser just before half-time.

articles.headline: Premier League VAR review: Should Man United's equalizing goal have been allowed?
articles.description: VAR often causes controversy, but how are decisions made? Our resident ref, Andy Davies, explains all.
articles.body:
The video assistant referee causes controversy every week, whether it be the Premier League, Champions League or FA Cup, but how are those decisions made and are they correct?

For the 2026-27 season, we are taking a look at the major incidents to explain the process in terms of both VAR protocol and the laws of the game. The most surprising, controversial and complicated decisions will be examined all season long right here.

Photo credit: USA Sports, NBC

 Andy Davies (@andydaviesref) is a former Select Group referee, with over 12 seasons on the elite list, working across the Premier League and Championship. With extensive experience at the elite level, he has operated within the VAR space in the Premier League and offers a unique insight into the processes, rationale and protocols that are delivered on a matchday. 

Did Lammens interfere with Suzuki?

Manchester United 4-4 Aston Villa (Nov. 8)

Referee: Chris Kavanagh

VAR: Craig Pawson

Time: 96 minutes

Incident: Possible foul in Manchester United's equalizing goal.

What happened: Bruno Fernandes swung in a last-chance corner kick as Man United threw every player they had on the pitch, including keeper Senne Lammens, into the penalty area.

Patrick Dorgu outjumped the Aston Villa defenders and, with keeper Zion Suzuki flapping at the ball, nodded home what seemed like a straightforward header into the net. However, Suzuki believed he was fouled by opposite number Lammens as the United No. 1 attempted to block the Villa keeper -- Lammens made contact with Suzuki while neither looking at the ball nor making any attempt to play it.

Referee Kavanagh was unmoved by the appeals, yellow-carding Suzuki for his protests and awarding the goal.

VAR decision: VAR checked and cleared the on-field decision of goal.

VAR review: VAR checked the incident and was comfortable that although Lammens clearly had intent to disturb Suzuki from having a clear path to punch the ball away by bumping into him, any contact was minimal and, more importantly, his impact on the Villa keeper was a 50-50 call. This is a ratio where VAR is not keen to get involved and will stick with the on-field decision.

Verdict: VAR were correct not to intervene in this situation as it fell short of the threshold for a clear on-field error.

Though Lammens' intention was obvious, intent is not a punishable offense, and the many replays didn't evidence enough of an impactful physical action on Suzuki that met the criteria for an intervention. However, Lammens did gamble with this play, and if referee Kavanagh had judged his action differently and awarded a late free kick to Villa, United could have few complaints.

This was a borderline call either way, and I am comfortable that the on-field decision should stick regardless of which way it fell.

Arsenal robbed of a penalty

Referee: Farai Hallam

VAR: Michael Oliver

Time: 42 minutes

Incident: Penalty not awarded to Arsenal for an offside offense.
